item.title: Sweat and Strawberry Jam - A Robotics Tale
item.description:
When you think of FIRST Robotics, do you think of fanfiction? Well, I do, thanks to my friend who decided to show me that :/

Allow me to explain the wonderful FRC fanfiction plot I’ve come up with, inspired by one of many overshipped couples on my team.

Characters

  • Todd (I might rename him Andy)
    • He’s a build lead on team 9265, the HiddenPIs. He’s hopelessly in love with a member of the programming department, who we shall detail next!
    • He struggles with Gender Dysphoria, and wonders what it would be like to be a woman
  • Eddy (I might rename him Mark)
    • He’s a programming member who loves playing around with prediction and consistency around Match Strategy, one day hoping his skills can help the team with alliance selections. He also has a small crush on Todd/Andy, though it’s not a feeling that he’s explored much.
    • He struggles with Gender Dysphoria, and wonders what it would be like to be a woman
  • Get it cause Andymark

Plot

We start on an offseason day near an offseason comp, where Todd/Andy is given the very important task of cleaning the Swerve Modules. He sees Eddy/Mark working on his prediction AI, and against his better judgment, goes over to flirt with him. One botched conversation later, Eddy/Mark is left with much more conflicted feelings about Todd/Andy, and the rest of the story is a secret synchronous race to get it worked out before build.

item.title: Welcome Intrusions Into The Lives We Lead
item.description:
Why Does This Exist?

Welcome Intrusions is my attempt at a modern literature work.

According to a poster I read, I suffer from a “fixed-mindset”, or whatever.

Does it suck? Yes. I have no idea how to keep the content from going insane by being cooked inside my own head, and whenever I try to solve this problem, I am assaulted by a barrage of AI tools that doesn’t allow me to breathe, let alone write a coherent story. All this work is, unfortunately, self-expression, and probably not good one at that. Maybe you’ll see it for more than what it is, or maybe not.
